paragraphs.source_en: Did Lady Kōdai truly mean everything she said? At times, Hideaki even harbored profound doubts about the Taikō: had his true wish really been, as Lady Kōdai claimed, to bring peace to the realm? Had he truly been so great a man? No, not necessarily. Perhaps he had sought nothing more than his own glory and advancement. Lady Kōdai, wishing only to glorify her late husband, had portrayed Ieyasu as a peerless hero.
